nuggets.title: Search returns docs user cannot access

scenario.symptoms: An employee asked the assistant about a confidential HR policy and received excerpts from executive-only docs. Vector search ranked by similarity only; ACL filter ran after top-k retrieval.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Embeddings index lacks per-chunk permission metadata enforced at query time. Post-filter shrinks results below k without backfill from allowed docs.

incident.headline: Retrieval returns forbidden chunks before ACL filtering

agenda.goal: Never surface document content the caller is not authorized to read.
agenda.opener: The bot quoted an executive-only doc—where should permissions be enforced in RAG?

evidence.strong: ACL-aware retrieval with filter at index query, over-fetch then filter with backfill, deny by default, audit logs.
evidence.adequate: Strip text in UI but chunks still retrieved in logs.

misconceptions.pattern: Asking the LLM not to mention secrets.
misconceptions.challenge: If forbidden text is already in the prompt context, is it truly protected?

probes: How do you index chunks for multi-tenant ACLs?
What if fewer than k docs pass the filter?
hints: Filter must happen before prompt assembly.
Metadata filters in vector DBs are common.
agenda.referenceFix: Store permission sets on each chunk, apply metadata filter during vector query, over-retrieve and backfill from allowed set, and block generation if insufficient authorized context.

scenario.symptoms: Support bot told customers an old refund policy after legal published an update. Search index refresh runs nightly; doc deletes are not tombstoned in the vector store.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Ingestion upserts new chunks but never deletes embeddings for removed paragraphs, so stale vectors still match queries.

incident.headline: Index updates without deletes leave obsolete embeddings searchable

agenda.goal: Keep retrieved knowledge in sync with source document lifecycle.
agenda.opener: Bot cited an old policy—how should indexing handle edits and deletes?

evidence.strong: Versioned doc ids, delete vectors on tombstone events, near-real-time incremental index, and cite source updated_at in answers.
evidence.adequate: Nightly full reindex without incremental deletes.

probes: How do you chunk a doc that changed one paragraph?
What SLA for legal policy updates?
hints: Treat delete as first-class index operation.
Chunk ids should include doc version.
agenda.referenceFix: Emit delete events for removed chunks, re-embed on version bump with stable chunk keys, stream index updates within minutes, and surface source timestamp to users.

scenario.symptoms: Users received confident wrong answers about API rate limits. Retrieval returned weak matches but the LLM still generated specifics not present in any chunk.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Prompt does not require citations or abstention when retrieval score is below threshold.

incident.headline: LLM fills gaps when retrieval confidence is too low

agenda.goal: Ensure answers stay grounded in retrieved evidence or refuse safely.
agenda.opener: Bot invented rate limits not in docs—how do you enforce grounding?

evidence.strong: Similarity threshold with abstain, cite-only prompting, answer validation against chunks, and logging retrieval scores.
evidence.adequate: Ask model to cite but no enforcement.
evidence.weak: Pure LLM completion after weak retrieval.

probes: What should the bot say when no chunk matches?
How do you detect hallucinations in eval?
hints: Low retrieval score should trigger refuse/clarify.
agenda.referenceFix: Reject generation below score threshold, require inline citations mapped to chunk ids, run post-check that claims appear in context, and return ‘I don’t know’ otherwise.
